newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 29.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
UNIFORM CIVIL CODE LEGISLATION RULED OUT

The government ruled out the possibility of bringing in legislation to enact a Uniform Civil Code. It told the Supreme Court it would not interfere on its own in the personal laws of minority communities. Bringing in a Uniform Civil Code would involve changes in personal laws of the minority communities and it was the policy not to interfere in the laws of the minority communities, counsel for the government said, quoting an affidavit. The affidavit had been filed in persuance to an apex court direction inquiring about efforts to secure a Uniform Civil Code.
The Pioneer
PRIME MINISTER PITCHES IN FOR BAHUJAN SAMAJ PARY LEADER

As the political stalemate in Uttar Pradesh continued, Prime Minister Deve Gowda made an effort to find support for Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) leader Mayawati within the United Front (UF). His attempt was just a week before a crucial meeting of the Congress Working Committee, which had been urging the UF to scale down its opposition to BSP leader's name for chief minister of the state. UF sources, however, said the Prime Minister's efforts were unlikely to succeed.
Indian Express
STRIKE DAMAGES COMMUNICATIONS NETWORK

The Intelligence Bureau said the post and telegraph employees' strike had severely damaged the communications network throughout the country because of a lack of maintenance. It said telex lines were badly affected and long-distance links to various locations had been snapped. Meanwhile, the cabinet decided to discuss the issue of removal of eligibility ceiling on the bonus for the striking employees.
The Economic Times
REGULATORY BODIES TO TAKE OVER STATE'S ROLE

The government will soon take steps to legally empower independent regulatory authorities to help the reform process in the infrastructure sector, Prime Minister Deve Gowda said. The state would increasingly give way to such regulatory authorities in infrastructure sectors such as power, transport and telecommunications, he added. Deve Gowda said the objective of the government was to bring in $10 billion of foreign direct investment annually, including investment in the infrastructure development.
BPL RESTRUCTURED INTO BUSINESS GROUPS

The 23 billion rupee BPL group has been restructured into six business groups. While T.P.G. Nambiar will continue to be the group chairman, operational responsibilities have been equally divided between his son A.G. Nambiar and son-in-law R. Chandrasekhar. Traditional group businesses -- entertainment electronics, appliances, components and related new ventures have come under the stewardship of A.G. Nambiar. Chandrasekhar has been given BPL's telecommunications and power businesses. He also gets the finance portfolio under the new organisational structure.
SANDOZ, CIBA GEIGY LIFE BUSINESS TO MERGE

Sandoz (India) will be merged into the life sciences business of Hindustan Ciba-Geigy (HCG). The speciality chemicals business of HCG is being demerged into a separate company. Sandoz shareholders will get 10 equity shares of 10 rupees each of HCG, to be renamed Novartis (India), for every 17 they hold in Sandoz. HCG shareholders will receive one 10 rupee share each in the new speciality chemical company, for every two 10 rupee shares held in Ciba.
NO WORD ON INSURANCE REFORMS IN COUNTRY REPORT

The country report prepared by government for the four-day World Infrastructure Forum Asia-1996 and the U.N. ESCAP Ministerial Conference falls short on the promise of opening up of the insurance sector. This is despite the fact the opening of insurance sector is necessary for generating long-term capital needed for funding infrastructure projects. The government's country report has only reiterated the Common Minimum Programme of the ruling United Front that experience gained in the working of the banking sector would be utilised for restructuring of the insurance industry.
Financial Express
FOREIGN BANKS EQUITY TO BE LIMITED IN DEPOSITORIES

The finance ministry was directed to limit the participation of foreign banks in the equity capital of depositories. Some members of parliament advised the finance minister against allowing foreign banks to pick up large stakes in stock depositories, sources said. Though no ban on equity participation is contemplated, the stock market regulator will be asked to consider a ceiling on the amount of equity that foreign banks can hold in depositories.
RATING SYSTEM SUGGESTED FOR INSURANCE COMPANIES
A rating system was suggested for insurance companies when the industry is finally thrown open to private companies. This is part of a report submitted to the Insurance Regulatory Authority.
MONTEK WANTS NO FIGURE-FUDGING IN FOREIGN-AIDED PROJECTS

Finance secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia has called the bluff on underprovisioning of budgetary resources for externally aided projects. He blamed unrealistic amounts set aside as additional central assistance for externally aided projects (EAP) for the gross under-utilisation of foreign assistance. Singh claimed inadequate allocation of funds on expenditure had led to a drop in external aid receipts. In fiscal 1993/94 (April-March), the shortfall was 16.91 billion rupees from a budgetary estimate of external assistance of 119.14 billion rupees. The gap was 15.02 billion rupees in 1994/95 and 27.75 billion rupees in 1995/96, Ahluwalia said, adding the problem was expected to surface more acutely in 1996/97.
Business Standard
PETRO-GOODS PRICES TO GO UP

The government plans to increase prices of subsidised petroleum products by 15 percent to bring them to par with international levels. This formed part of the government's approach to deregulating the country's oil sector. Though prices were raised in July to bring them closer to international prices, they were still 15 percent short.
MORE ITEMS UNDER SPECIAL IMPORT LICENSE PLANNED

The commerce ministry plans to expand the special import licence (SIL) list. More items permitted for import through SIL means more premium on the licence, which acts as an incentive for exporters. The ministry has already reduced the items on the negative list six times in the current year to increase incentives. This has also been done in view of the gradual phasing out of quantative restrictions and replacing them ith tariffs in the long run.
CAIRN TO REPLACE COMMAND IN RAVVA FIELD

Cairn Energy of the U.K. will replace Command Petroleum as Videocon's partner for developing the Ravva oilfield. Marubeni and the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation are the other two firms in the four-company joint venture. Australia's Command, which holds 22.5 percent in the venture, has has been taken over by Cairn Energy in a deal this month. Consequently, all assets of Command, including holdings in foreign joint ventures, will be transferred to Cairn Energy. This is the second instance of a change in ownership pattern in a joint venture after developed medium-sized oilfields were opened to the private sector after 1992.
PRATT & WHITNEY CONSIDERS ENGINE PARTS FACILITY

Aircraft engine manufacturer Pratt & Whitney is weighing its options on setting up a manufacturing facility for aircraft engine components in India. The investment for the project is estimated at $100 million. If the project takes shape, the U.S. company's participation could be in the form of equity participation or a joint venture, though other options are not ruled out. The company denied that the setting up of its plant is dependent on Boeing getting the requisite orders from the Indian flag carrier, Air India.
